overview: Cambodia is a country in mainland South-East Asia. Its capital and largest city is Phnom Penh. From the 800s to the 1400s it was the centre of the Khmer Empire, which built Angkor Wat, the largest religious monument in the world. In the late 1970s the Khmer Rouge regime caused the deaths of around 1.5 to 2 million people. Khmer is the official language.

geography.text: Much of Cambodia is a low, flat basin around the Tonlé Sap, the largest freshwater lake in South-East Asia. In the rainy season the Mekong floods so strongly that the Tonlé Sap river reverses its flow and the lake grows several times larger. Forested hills and mountains rise around the edges, and the country has a short coast on the Gulf of Thailand.

history.text: The Khmer Empire, centred on Angkor, dominated much of mainland South-East Asia between the 800s and the 1400s. Cambodia later became a French protectorate and won independence in 1953. In 1975 the Khmer Rouge took power and caused the deaths of around 1.5 to 2 million people before being driven out in 1979. Peace and UN-run elections followed in the 1990s.

events.title: Khmer Empire founded
events.text: Jayavarman II declares himself universal king.

events.title: Angkor Wat
events.text: King Suryavarman II builds Angkor Wat.

events.title: Khmer Rouge
events.text: The Khmer Rouge seize power; their rule ends in 1979.

events.title: UN elections
events.text: UN-organised elections follow a peace agreement.

government.text: Cambodia is a constitutional monarchy with a king as head of state. In practice the Cambodian People's Party has dominated politics since the 1980s. Hun Sen was Prime Minister for almost 40 years and handed power to his son, Hun Manet, in 2023.

economy.text: Clothing and shoe factories are Cambodia's biggest export industry, along with rice, tourism and construction. It uses both its own currency, the riel, and the US dollar.

culture.text: The temples of Angkor, including Angkor Wat, the largest religious monument in the world, show the power of the old Khmer Empire. Angkor Wat appears on Cambodia's flag. Khmer classical dance, performed by dancers in elaborate costumes, is listed by UNESCO.

items.title: Angkor Wat
items.text: Built in the 1100s as a Hindu temple, later Buddhist.

items.title: Royal ballet
items.text: Classical Khmer dance, listed by UNESCO.

sport.text: Football and kun Khmer, a form of kickboxing, are popular. Cambodia hosted the Southeast Asian Games for the first time in 2023.

items.text: Phnom Penh hosted the Southeast Asian Games.
